clearedSpotChecks.check: Lead L-1087: the definition of erigon v3.8.1 IntraBlockState.ReadStamp and whether a per-frame cached SLOAD can serve the outer PoolManager frame a stale word after a hook reenters (src/PoolManager.sol:153-159, 196-202).
clearedSpotChecks.note: Fetched read_paths.go, journal.go, interpreter.go, instructions.go, operations_acl.go and intra_block_state.go at v3.8.1 from raw.githubusercontent.com. ReadStamp returns {len(journal.entries), journal.epoch} (read_paths.go 1789-1803). journal.Reset and journal.revert both do epoch++ (journal.go 115-143), and intra_block_state.go 2592 bumps the epoch on storage commit. lookupSlot (interpreter.go 113-131) returns a hit only when the saved stamp equals the current one. The memo path in opSload (instructions.go 771-777) skips the stamp check only when memoGen equals cacheGen, and cacheGen is incremented once per dispatched opcode (interpreter.go 587), so the memo set by gasSLoadEIP2929 (operations_acl.go 142) serves only the execute phase of the same SLOAD, with no state change between. In the SSTORE gas function (operations_acl.go 60-97) the cold path warms the slot before it reads and stores the value under the post-warm stamp, and the SetState that follows appends a journal entry and invalidates it. The per-frame slots are cleared when a context is reused (interpreter.go 219-221) and the cache is enabled per frame (interpreter.go 515). Since the journal only shrinks through revert, which moves the epoch, an equal stamp implies no journalled change in between. The outer reads of slot0 at src/PoolManager.sol:154 and inside Pool.swap after beforeSwap at :202 therefore see the current word. The unjournalled-change list was taken from the code comment and the epoch sites found by grep; I did not audit every IntraBlockState mutator for a missing journal append.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Lead L-1086, Nethermind part: the four Nethermind 2.2.2 jump destination kernels against the scalar rule on the PoolManager runtime and about 1.1 million other inputs.
clearedSpotChecks.note: JumpDestinationAnalyzer.cs at tag 2.2.2 (740 lines, fetched) dispatches at lines 156-159 exactly as stated: Avx512Vbmi with Vector512.IsHardwareAccelerated and length >= 64, Avx2 from 32, Ssse3 from 16, AdvSimd.Arm64 from 16, else scalar. The Vector512 kernel has the PUSH1-run carry path (lines 216-245) the research names, with signed sbyte comparisons against PUSH1 and PUSHx so bytes 0x80 and above count as non-push. I did not rerun the C port. Its result covers the deployed bytes, and the planted-fault runs show the harness detects errors. The residual gap is the .NET JIT lowering, which the research leaves as a low lead; a fault there would cause a client fork, not a fund movement.

clearedSpotChecks.note: With an anonymous ghcr.io pull token I fetched the v2.11.0 image index (amd64 manifest sha256:973f432f1c625..., attestation manifest sha256:cd6c86fc28b24...) and its provenance layer, which records VERGEN_GIT_SHA b9abbcc1b982755baa9021e6874e2e58936ca65f, VERGEN_GIT_DESCRIBE v2.11.0 and VERGEN_GIT_DIRTY false. Cargo.lock at that commit and at tag v2.11.0 have the same sha256 (5cc28d67...) and pin evm2 0.1.0 and ruint 1.21.1. On 2026-11-26 eth.api.pocket.network answered web3_clientVersion reth/v2.11.0-b9abbcc/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu and eth_getCode of 0x000000000004444c5dc75cB358380D2e3dE08A90 at latest gave 24,009 bytes with sha256 prefix 3316c7b1c67095ef, matching networks.json. ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com returned a Cloudflare challenge page, as the research says. The binary behind the endpoint cannot be inspected, so identity rests on the version string, as the research states.
